source.quote: Berkeley Audio Design's own page for the Alpha DAC Reference Series 3P, read 2026-11-24, specification list: « Input sampling rate: 32kHz to 192kHz »; « Input word length: 24-bit »; « Digital Inputs: AES - XLR, 110; SPDIF1 - BNC, 75; SPDIF2 - BNC, 75; TOSLINK - Toslink optical connector »; « Ultra low phase noise Precision Clocking at 44.1kHz, 48kHz, 88.2kHz, 96kHz, 176.4kHz and 192kHz sampling rates +/- 100 ppm »; « MQA Rendering and multiple digital filter options ». Self-description: « The Perfected Technology Alpha DAC Reference Series 3P achieves a level of time domain Accuracy ». The same page carries the earlier Series 3 text, where the maker writes « Multiple digital filter options », « MQA rendering automatically detects MQA Core decoded signals and performs MQA rendering to 384kHz and above », « 99+% of modern DAC's, including the Alpha DAC Reference Series 3, use multi-bit D/A converters » and, on DSD, « Virtually all reproduction of DSD files using external DAC's is with a computer based music server as the source », recommending conversion of DSD to PCM in the computer.

_this_dac_has_no_usb_input_and_that_is_t: The spec list enumerates FOUR digital inputs - AES/XLR, two S/PDIF on BNC, TOSLINK - and no USB. The maker sells the USB input as a separate box: the Products menu lists « Alpha USB Reference Series » and « Alpha USB Series 2 » beside the DACs. So the first high-end record in this catalogue whose USB ceiling is not low, not unknown, but ABSENT BY DESIGN - there is no socket. Nothing in the schema says that. `inputs.usb` simply has no block, which reads as « nobody filled it in » and is indistinguishable from a page that forgot to mention USB. A consumer asking « what can I send this over USB » gets silence where it should get « this device has no USB input; the maker sells one ».
_no_input_block_because_the_maker_rates_: « Input sampling rate: 32kHz to 192kHz » is ONE line for the whole converter, in a spec list that names its four inputs separately just below. Ferrum's WANDLA, written an hour earlier, proves a maker differentiates when it means to: six inputs, six ratings. Berkeley does not differentiate, so no per-input block is written here and 192000/24 is recorded at device level. The cost is visible: this catalogue has no way to say « all inputs alike at 192 », only « the device does 192 » plus four inputs rated nothing. 31 of 63 records have input blocks; this is the 33rd without one, and the first where the absence is the maker's choice rather than the page's silence.
_optical_at_192_would_have_been_the_outl: If the global line were read per input, TOSLINK would land at 192 kHz - against 96 on five other makers, for which vocabulary/why-the-optical-default-stays-low exists. It is NOT recorded, because the maker never says it about the optical input. Worth naming so nobody later reads the absence as a measurement.
_multi_bit_is_not_a_technology_value: « 99+% of modern DAC's, including the Alpha DAC Reference Series 3, use multi-bit D/A converters » is the only converter wording on the page, and it is a statement about the industry that happens to include this device. `multi-bit` is not one of the four values `technology` takes: in chip language it most often means a multi-bit delta-sigma, as opposed to 1-bit, and it does NOT mean a resistor ladder - but the page does not settle which. family is `unknown` and technology is left ABSENT, which means a consumer's cascade falls back to delta_sigma. That fallback happens to be the likely reading here, and it is still a fallback, not a fact.
_filters_named_nowhere: « multiple digital filter options » twice, on both the 3P and the Series 3 text, and not one filter is named. No device_settings is written: « multiple » is a count the maker will not give. This is the fourth selectable-filter device in the catalogue after RME's five, Totaldac's compensation filter and Ferrum's two-three-four, and the second whose count the maker withholds. internal_bypass, modelled around a rate threshold, still stands on one record.
_dsd_absent_not_unknown: The spec list gives rates and word length and says nothing of DSD; elsewhere the maker tells the user to convert DSD to PCM in the computer before sending it. That is advice about a workflow, not a statement that the input refuses DSD. So no dsd field is written at all - neither a rate nor `unknown` - because the page asks the question and never closes it.
